Hi Elena / Stratum infra team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a quick baseline ask so we can align on Dedicated capacity sizing: I attached the token profile you exported and annotated the fields I used. Key points you mentioned: average response ~120 tokens, 95th percentile response ~600 tokens for longer agent flows, expected peak concurrency ~220 concurrent requests during product events, and p95 latency target = 250ms.

Quick ask from our side: can you confirm the following from your telemetry (or the attached CSV):
- peak RPS observed in last 30 days (15-min max)
- average tokens per request and 95th percentile tokens per request (you already gave ballparks; want raw sample)
- whether requests are single-turn or multi-turn with KV cache reuse (establish effective tokens/sec impact)

What I’ll do after you confirm is run a capacity sketch mapping tokens/sec to GPU counts for two SKU options (A100-80GB equivalent and an L40-like cost-optimized variant) and give three scenarios: baseline sustained, event-window peak, and 2x headroom recommendation for safe rollouts.

Attachment: stratum_token_profile.csv (please update if any numbers differ).

If you prefer, we can do a short sizing call tomorrow 30 min to walk numbers.

Thanks,

Thanks Priyom — attaching the CSV you requested (same filename) with the 30d telemetry slice. Notes from our side:
- 15-min max RPS observed = 75 requests/sec (during product marketing demo on 2027-10-18)
- Average tokens/request = 120 (median), p95 tokens/request = 540
- Traffic is a mix: ~70% single-turn conversational queries, ~30% multi-turn where we reuse KV cache across 3–6 turns in a short session
- Typical prompt + system tokens add ~40 tokens overhead per request
- Model variant: off-the-shelf open-model fine-tuned (non-quantized in prod today); we are evaluating 4-bit quantized variants for cost savings but worried about tail latency

We want to keep p95 <= 250ms and p99 < 500ms. For the upcoming Q1 launch we expect sustained RPS around 40 req/s with spikes to the 75 req/s window above. Please include the impact of multi-turn KV cache reuse — it should reduce overall tokens/sec by ~20% for sessions that reuse cache (we measured in-house).

Attaching: stratum_token_profile.csv, draft SLA (stratum-sla-draft.pdf).

Best,

Subject: Re: Stratum Dedicated Fit & Burst Margin — throughput vs. SLO tradeoffs

Elena — thanks for the telemetry, that’s very helpful. I ran a short mapping and summarized below so we have concrete numbers to discuss on a sizing call. I’ll attach the workbook (priyom_dedicated-sizing.xlsx) with the line-by-line math. High-level assumptions I used:
- Tokens per GPU throughput: baseline (non-quantized large model) ~30k tokens/sec per A100-80GB equiv with our runtime and continuous batching; quantized (4-bit) variant ~48k tokens/sec (efficiency gain varies by model).
- Effective tokens/sec reduction for KV-reuse flows: 20% discount on tokens/sec demand for that fraction of sessions (per your note).
- Latency SLO target: p95 <= 250ms — that constraints our continuous batching window (we assume 8–12ms per token in hot-path; numbers baked into workbook).

Scenario table (rounded):
- Sustained baseline (expected steady run Q1): 40 RPS * 120 tokens = 4,800 tokens/sec. After KV reuse mix (-20% on 30% of traffic) => ~4,400 tokens/sec.
  - GPUs needed (non-quantized, 30k tps/GPU): 1 GPU (4,400/30k ~ 0.15) — but we recommend minimum 2 GPUs for redundancy and model-hotshard distribution.
- Event-window peak (15-min max seen): 75 RPS * 540 p95 tokens ~ 40,500 tokens/sec. Adjust for KV reuse mix => ~37,900 tokens/sec.
  - GPUs needed (non-quantized): ~1.27 GPU equivalents -> practically 2 GPUs if running single-slab, but because of latency and scheduling, we recommend 4 GPUs to keep within p95 250ms during sustained peak bursts (this gives ~2.5x headroom over raw compute requirement to keep batching windows small).
- Safe production headroom (2x safety factor on peak): target runway ~76k tokens/sec => recommend a 6-GPU slab on non-quantized SKU or a 4-GPU slab if you commit to the 4-bit quantized variant (48k tps/GPU), with staged rollout to validate tail latency.

Notes / tradeoffs:
- Quantized variant reduces GPU count materially (6->4) but increases p99 tail risk; we can mitigate with smaller batching windows and KV-caching warm-up.
- For Dedicated we can provision a 4-GPU slab initially behind autoscaling/burst gates and pop to 6 GPUs for event windows. That aligns with an ops policy rather than permanent reserve and reduces commit cost.
- If you require strict p95 headroom without autoscale, commit to 6 GPUs on A100-equivalent non-quantized SKU.

Next steps I propose:
1) 30-min sizing call to walk the workbook and confirm peak SLO tradeoffs (Karthik + Monica will join to cover ops & pricing).
2) If you want a conservative purchase/commit quote, we’ll price the 6-GPU slab and an alternate 4-GPU quantized option with performance caveats.
3) We’ll run a 48-hour pilot with a mirrored traffic replay to validate p95/p99 and cold-start behavior.

Propose Wed 2027-12-02 14:00 PT for the call — please confirm.

Thanks,
Priyom

Elena — looping in to confirm we’ll bring ops + pricing to the call. Quick clarifications from our side before the meeting:
- Can you share expected launch cadence (soft launch vs. wide) and preferred commitment model (monthly reserved slab vs. Dedicated with autoscale guards)? That will change our recommendation between a permanent 6-GPU commit vs. a smaller reserved slab + scheduled burst capacity.
- For the pilot, please provide a 24–48h trace replay or a representative traffic dump; we’ll run it on a mirrored slab to measure tail latency and token throughput under realistic cache warm-up conditions.

We’ll prepare two commercial options for the call: (A) conservative non-quantized commit (6 A100-equivalent GPUs) and (B) optimized quantized commit (4 GPUs) with an ops playbook to keep p99 risk acceptable. Pricing + uplift for burst policy will be ready in the call deck.
